items.title: Arturo O'Farrill interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 6, 2024
items.q: because Andy did that. He sat me down and played me the history of Latin piano players.

ctx.x: Well I was definitely madly in love with “Hymn of the Seventh Galaxy” which is the Chick Corea recording. I must have worn that thing to death. I was also madly in love with “Innervisions” — Stevie Wonder’s “Innervisions.” And I was also madly — I had by the way kind of rejected Latin music as there’s something about being in New York at that period in my school in that neighborhood that made me — it “othered” me, being Latino. It othered me being Mexican, being Cuban. And so I ran as far as I could from that…

You’d learn to be a jazz musician by (a) listening intently — I was a Bud Powell freak — I listened to nothing but Bud Powell, and then just by osmosis, hanging out with those older jazz musicians, and then of course we would play any gig we could get. So that was about the age of 16 was that part of my life. And I didn’t embrace anything remotely Latin ‘til years later when I met to the great bassist Andy Gonzalez and he told me…

I think that when I listen — of course pan-Latin music — I’ve had a lot of trouble knowing where I am. And I’ve used this excuse with me that oh this music you really need to have lived when you were a kid. You need to hear it from the time you’re a child to really embrace it. And it’s probably not true.
